newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan sees single-digit inflation in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan sees single-digit inflation in 1997.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said inflation would slow to around 9 percent in 1997, the lowest rate since 1957, a newspaper said.
"Brazil had single digit inflation only in 1947, 1948 and 1957. We are in a position to achieve that again in 1997," Malan was quoted as saying by O Globo newspaper.
He said the conditions for consolidating low inflation are not incompatible with economic growth, according to O Globo.
Recently, Brazil's multitude of inflation indices have been falling and some have even registered deflation in prices.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
